title: Push-and-turn child-resistant closure for medicine containers
abstract: A container cap with an inner and outer shell. The user must press down on the cap while rotating it so that locking lugs on the inner shell disengage from the bottle neck. A toddler lacks the coordinated force and dexterity to press and turn at the same time, so the container stays closed.

title: Squeeze-and-turn safety cap with deformable side tabs
abstract: A closure whose side walls carry flexible tabs. Squeezing the tabs releases a ratchet that otherwise prevents unscrewing. The closure is child-resistant because squeezing and rotating must be performed together, while remaining usable by adults with moderate hand strength.

title: Blister pack with peel-and-push opening for single tablets
abstract: A medication blister pack in which an outer paper layer must first be peeled back before a tablet can be pushed through the foil. The two-step action limits how many tablets a young child can release and reduces accidental ingestion.

title: Bittering agents to deter accidental poisoning in children
abstract: Review of denatonium benzoate as an aversive additive in household chemicals and cleaning products. The extremely bitter taste causes children to spit out the liquid, reducing the volume swallowed. Evidence on effectiveness in preventing poisoning is mixed.

title: Flow-restricting insert for bottle necks limiting liquid discharge rate
abstract: An insert placed in the neck of a bottle containing a narrow channel that slows the discharge of liquid. A child tipping the bottle receives only a small volume per tilt, giving time for an adult to intervene. The insert is fixed and requires no lock or cap manipulation.

title: Magnetic cabinet latch released by a key magnet
abstract: A concealed latch inside a cabinet door that opens only when a separate magnetic key is held against the outside of the door. Used to keep household chemicals and medicines out of reach of children without visible mechanical locks.

title: Evaluation of child-resistant packaging standards and real-world failure rates
abstract: A study of how often children aged 42 to 51 months can open packaging that meets child-resistance test standards. Many closures are defeated by persistent children, and some adults disable the mechanism by leaving caps unsecured, highlighting the need for designs that are easy to re-close.

title: Smart pill dispenser with biometric authentication and timed release
abstract: An electronic dispenser that releases a single scheduled dose only after fingerprint verification. A motorised carousel holds the tablets, and a companion app logs each dispensing event and alerts caregivers when a dose is missed.

title: Tablet dispensing cap that releases one unit per inversion
abstract: A cap containing a rotating metering wheel with a single pocket. Each time the bottle is inverted and returned upright, one tablet drops into the pocket and is released through a side opening. Limits the number of tablets obtainable in a short time.

title: Tilt-angle sensing in handheld containers using low-cost accelerometers
abstract: Experiments showing that inexpensive MEMS accelerometers can detect the tilt angle and tapping of a handheld container with high accuracy. Proposed applications include smart packaging, spill alerts and usage tracking for consumer products.

title: Pinch-lock lid for food storage boxes
abstract: A storage box lid with hinged clips that must be pinched inward on both sides at once to open. Designed for easy use by adults while making it difficult for infants to open the box.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation for question answering over scientific documents
abstract: This work combines dense retrieval with a large language model so that answers are grounded in retrieved passages. Experiments show reduced hallucination compared with generation alone on scientific question answering benchmarks.

title: Self-cleaning coating for photovoltaic panels using hydrophobic nanoparticles
abstract: A transparent coating applied to solar panels causes water droplets to roll off and carry dust away. The coating maintains light transmission above ninety percent and reduces cleaning frequency in dusty regions.

title: Tortuous micro-channel geometries for passive flow control of viscous and granular media
abstract: Analysis of serpentine and zig-zag channels that reduce the flow rate of liquids and granular solids without moving parts. Channel width, bend angle and surface roughness are shown to control discharge rate, with applications in dosing and packaging.
